purpose: Why a fleet state exists, for the states where the honest answer is counterintuitive and the intuitive fix is destructive. Keyed by the reason codes fleet_doctor emits; every code carries a row and every row is cited by a code.

agents_dir_unreadable.summary: The LaunchAgent directory could not be listed.
agents_dir_unreadable.why: Every generation, delivery and drain fact is read from installed LaunchAgents. With the directory unreadable there is no evidence at all, which is reported as unknown rather than as an empty host.
agents_dir_unreadable.remedy: Check the path and its permissions, then re-run. Treat every other finding in this run as unverified.
agents_dir_unreadable.do_not: Do not read an unreadable agents directory as a host with no agents.

census_complete.why: Runners register at repository scope or at organization scope, and the repository endpoint omits organization runners without saying so. Only a census that read both can be quoted as capacity.

census_identity_authenticated.summary: The capacity census CLI reaches GitHub as an authenticated identity.
census_identity_authenticated.why: Only an authenticated identity can read runner registrations reliably; the check reads the free rate_limit endpoint with the census's own repository binding.

census_identity_unauthenticated.summary: The capacity census CLI reaches GitHub anonymously (60/hour ceiling).
census_identity_unauthenticated.why: An anonymous census shares one 60/hour allowance with every host behind the same IP, runs it out within minutes of a --plan loop, and then reports every required label as capacity unknown, which refuses pool drain/off.
census_identity_unauthenticated.remedy: Run with TARTCI_GH_CLI=ghapp (the default when ghapp is installed), or repair the CLI's GitHub login.
census_identity_unauthenticated.do_not: Do not change GitHub App permissions or org settings for this; the identity, not the permission, is wrong.

census_identity_unknown.summary: The census CLI did not report a core rate-limit ceiling, so its identity is unproven.
census_identity_unknown.why: A CLI that will not answer the free rate_limit probe leaves the identity unproven; that is neither authenticated nor anonymous.
census_identity_unknown.remedy: Run `<cli> api rate_limit` by hand with GH_REPO=<repo> to see what it returns.

census_incomplete.summary: A registration scope could not be read.
census_incomplete.why: The scope that failed is exactly where a missing runner might live, so a label absent from an incomplete census is unknown, never unserved. A smaller number reads as a confident finding and is the more dangerous error.
census_incomplete.remedy: Restore access to the failed endpoint and re-run before making any capacity decision.
census_incomplete.do_not: Do not quote the partial count as the runner population.

census_module_unavailable.summary: The dual-scope census module is absent from this support root.
census_module_unavailable.why: Reading only the repository endpoint would produce a confident undercount, so no census is reported rather than a single-scope one.
census_module_unavailable.remedy: Install a support generation that carries scripts/runner_census.py, or pass --no-census to state that capacity was deliberately not measured.

census_repo_unknown.summary: No managed lane declares a runner repository.
census_repo_unknown.why: Census targets are derived from each installed lane's own TARTCI_RUNNER_REPO, because the plist is what launchd hands the supervisor. With none declared there is no target to measure.
census_repo_unknown.remedy: Pass --repo OWNER/REPO explicitly, or check that the installed lane plists still carry their runner environment.

delivery_unknown.summary: Some agent declares no resolvable program.
delivery_unknown.why: Whether a staged generation reaches this host depends entirely on what its agents exec. An agent whose program cannot be resolved makes the answer unknown for the whole host.
delivery_unknown.remedy: Inspect the named LaunchAgent's ProgramArguments before planning a deploy.
delivery_unknown.do_not: Do not start a deploy on the assumption that the unresolved agent behaves like its siblings.

effective_generation_matches.summary: Every managed agent executes the cohort the receipt records as installed.
effective_generation_matches.why: Installed and effective are separate facts. They agree here, which is the only state in which a receipt can be read as a statement about what runs.

effective_generation_mismatch.summary: The host executes a different cohort than the one it records as installed.
effective_generation_mismatch.why: Staging a generation writes a receipt whether or not anything execs it. A host in this state runs old code while every receipt, exit code and status line reports the new one, so the fix an operator believes they shipped was never delivered.
effective_generation_mismatch.remedy: Deliver the cohort by the route this host actually execs, then re-run and confirm effective matches installed. For a sealed launcher host see sealed_launcher_bundle.
effective_generation_mismatch.do_not: Do not treat the install receipt, or a zero exit from the installer, as evidence that the new code is running.

fleet_not_ready.summary: The authoritative support root reports the fleet not ready.
fleet_not_ready.why: The named problem code is the machine-readable cause and is the thing to act on; the word NO by itself has sent operators to rebuild parts that were never broken.
fleet_not_ready.remedy: Act on the reported problem code, not on the readiness verdict.

fleet_ready.summary: The installed generation reports the fleet ready.
fleet_ready.why: Readiness is reported from the installed generation because that is the tree the running supervisors execute.

generation_path_exec.summary: Agents exec a generation path directly, so a staged generation reaches them.
generation_path_exec.why: This is the delivery shape in which install means what it appears to mean: the next generation replaces what execs.

hold_receipt_malformed.summary: The held-idle receipt could not be read, or is not exactly held-idle.
hold_receipt_malformed.why: The receipt is compared exactly. A near-miss is not a weaker yes, it is a no, and drain will refuse on it.
hold_receipt_malformed.remedy: Resolve the file's state before attempting a drain.
hold_receipt_malformed.do_not: Do not write the receipt by hand to make this pass. See persistent_runners_without_hold_receipt.

hold_receipt_present.summary: Persistent listeners are covered by an exact held-idle receipt.
hold_receipt_present.why: The receipt authorizes exactly one drain era and is invalidated when the pool reopens.

installed_generation_unknown.summary: Managed agents are installed but no readable receipt says which cohort they should execute.
installed_generation_unknown.why: Without an installed identity there is nothing to compare the executed cohort against, so the comparison is unknown rather than passing by default.
installed_generation_unknown.remedy: Restore or re-write the install receipt before judging what this host runs.

lane_lease_never_fits.summary: A lane's VM is larger than the lease budget it is admitted against.
lane_lease_never_fits.why: The lease store would deny this VM even on an idle host, so the lane can never boot. It stops polling for work and says so instead of scanning the queue and asking Shipyard every minute for a VM it cannot start.
lane_lease_never_fits.remedy: Shrink the lane's VM (TARTCI_MACOS_VM_CORES / vm_pool_cores) to fit the budget, or give the host a larger lease universe. The finding names the requested cores and the budget.
lane_lease_never_fits.do_not: Do not disable the lease store or raise the gate reserve to make the lane boot; the budget exists to keep agent cores.

lanes_exceed_lease_capacity.summary: More identical lanes are installed than the lease budget can run at once.
lanes_exceed_lease_capacity.why: A lane beyond the budget's capacity can only boot while a sibling is idle, and then the sibling would have served. It adds queue polling and admission calls but no concurrent capacity (m5: two 12-core gate lanes in a 14-core universe). While a sibling holds a VM the extra lane waits locally without scanning or asking Shipyard.
lanes_exceed_lease_capacity.remedy: Remove the extra lane from the host's fleet profile, or size the VMs so the budget holds every lane at once.
lanes_exceed_lease_capacity.do_not: Do not treat the extra lane as spare capacity when planning the fleet.

lease_fit_ok.summary: Every measured lane can lease its VM, and identical lanes can run together.
lease_fit_ok.why: Each lane records its own lease-fit verdict against the lease store's capacity model.

lease_fit_unmeasured.summary: No lane has recorded a lease-fit verdict yet.
lease_fit_unmeasured.why: Lanes write the verdict each poll; a host whose supervisors predate lease-fit, or that has not polled since install, has none.
lease_fit_unmeasured.remedy: Wait one poll after the lanes start, or update the host's tartci.

no_installed_profile.summary: This host has no installed macOS fleet profile.
no_installed_profile.why: Only a host that installed a fleet profile can drift from its checked-in source; the check has nothing to compare here.

no_managed_launchagents.summary: No managed fleet LaunchAgent is installed.
no_managed_launchagents.why: With no receipt either, this host is simply not a managed fleet host. With a receipt present it is a real fault: something records a cohort that nothing executes.
no_managed_launchagents.remedy: If a receipt exists, install the fleet lanes or remove the stale receipt.

no_persistent_runners.summary: No persistent Actions listener is installed, so drain terminalizes on provider agents alone.
no_persistent_runners.why: Ephemeral providers finish their current job and then wait at the admission gate, which is a safe local drain primitive. Only a stock persistent listener lacks one.

persistent_runners_without_hold_receipt.summary: Drain will refuse, and it refuses after the host is already opted out.
persistent_runners_without_hold_receipt.why: A stock persistent Actions listener has no safe local drain primitive: worker absence misses the interval between a job being accepted and its worker spawning, so stopping on that evidence can kill a running job. Draining safely requires removing the host from routing and publishing a held-idle receipt only once the scheduler reports every persistent runner idle. No supported producer ships that receipt today. Drain writes participation=0 and pool-state=draining before it discovers this, so a refusal leaves the host opted out with its agents still loaded.
persistent_runners_without_hold_receipt.remedy: Do not begin a drain on this host. If one has already refused, return the host to service with tartci pool on, which also invalidates any stale hold receipt.
persistent_runners_without_hold_receipt.do_not: Do not create the held-idle receipt by hand. It asserts that a scheduler observed every persistent runner idle. Writing it locally asserts an observation nothing made, and authorizes stopping a listener that may be holding a live job.

profile_drift.summary: The installed fleet profile differs from the checked-in profile with the same name.
profile_drift.why: Every receipt check verifies the installed copy against itself, so a host edited in place, or installed before the checked-in profile moved on, passes all of them while running settings nobody reviewed (for example a missing github_api_timeout_seconds silently reverting to the 15-second default).
profile_drift.remedy: Decide which side is right. Reinstall from the checked-in profile with `tartci fleet-macos install <profile> --apply` (drain first), or commit the host's edit to profiles/.
profile_drift.do_not: Do not hand-edit the installed profile to match; the receipt and rendered plists would then disagree with it.

profile_drift_unknown.summary: The installed profile could not be compared with a checked-in source.
profile_drift_unknown.why: An unparsable profile, a missing `name`, zero or several checked-in profiles with that name, or no tomllib interpreter all leave the comparison unanswered, which is not the same as in sync.
profile_drift_unknown.remedy: Run `tartci fleet-macos profile-drift` for the specific reason.

profile_in_sync.summary: The installed fleet profile matches its checked-in source key for key.
profile_in_sync.why: Receipts bind the installed copy to itself, so only a comparison against the checked-in profile carrying the same name can say the host runs what the repository describes.

program_unresolvable.summary: The executed cohort could not be resolved for some agent.
program_unresolvable.why: The executed cohort is read from ProgramArguments and, for a signed launcher, from the bundle's sealed metadata. When neither can be read the agent's identity is unknown, which must not be reported as agreement.
program_unresolvable.remedy: Inspect the named LaunchAgent and its program before trusting any generation claim for this host.

readiness_not_managed.summary: This host carries no managed fleet profile.
readiness_not_managed.why: Legacy and provider-only hosts are legitimate. Readiness does not apply to them and is not reported as a failure.

readiness_probe_failed.why: The probe needs a Python 3.11 or newer interpreter with tomllib and a support root that carries the readiness script. macOS ships 3.9, so a stock interpreter fails the probe. Reporting that as not ready would invent a fleet fault out of a missing interpreter.
readiness_probe_failed.remedy: Set TARTCI_PYTHON to a 3.11+ interpreter, or check that the support root named in the receipt still exists.

readiness_verdict_depends_on_invocation.summary: Two support roots on this host return different readiness verdicts for the same fleet.
readiness_verdict_depends_on_invocation.why: Readiness is computed against a support root, and the support root comes from whichever copy of the CLI asked. A git checkout and the installed generation therefore disagree at the same instant, each correct about the tree it measured and each read as a statement about the fleet. A checkout reports receipt_mismatch because the receipt names the installed generation's root, not the checkout's.
readiness_verdict_depends_on_invocation.remedy: Read the installed generation's verdict as authoritative, since that is the tree the running supervisors execute. Run the installed CLI, not a checkout, when asking whether the fleet is up.
readiness_verdict_depends_on_invocation.do_not: Do not report a checkout's readiness verdict as the host's.

sealed_launcher_bundle.summary: This host execs a sealed launcher bundle, so a generation stage alone cannot change what it runs.
sealed_launcher_bundle.why: Agents exec a signed Developer ID app, and that app runs its own sealed copy of the support cohort from inside the bundle. Staging a newer generation beside it succeeds, writes a receipt and exits 0 while the bundle keeps executing the cohort it was sealed around. This is how a host silently misses every fix it appears to have received.
sealed_launcher_bundle.remedy: Deliver a re-signed launcher bundle built around the new cohort and install with --launch-helper-source, refreshing the pinned approval digest, then confirm the executed cohort matches the installed one.
sealed_launcher_bundle.do_not: Do not read a zero exit from fleet-macos install --apply on this host as evidence that the new generation is running.

self_update_current.summary: This host runs main's tartci, or its undeployed commits are recent and the last self-update did not fail.
self_update_current.why: Hosts fell weeks behind main unnoticed; tartci's skew is measured against first-parent main and shown here even when the self-update agent is off.

self_update_problem.summary: This host runs stale tartci code, its skew could not be measured, or the last self-update failed.
self_update_problem.why: A host behind main runs fixes the rest of the fleet has; a failed self-update leaves the host serving the previous generation, which is safe but must be seen.
self_update_problem.remedy: Read `tartci fleet-macos self-update --status` and the receipt under ~/.tartci/state/self-update/attempts, then run `tartci fleet-macos self-update --plan`.
self_update_problem.do_not: Do not hand-install from a shared working copy; the self-update path installs from its own clean checkout of main.

self_update_unmeasured.summary: tartci's skew against main was never measured here.
self_update_unmeasured.why: The launchd watchdog re-measures it every 30 minutes on a managed host; until then the answer is unknown, not current.

supply_match.summary: Every registration this host's installed profile mints matches the published declared supply.
supply_match.why: The published fleet/advertised-labels.json is what other projects read to learn which labels this fleet serves; it is generated from git, so only a comparison with the installed profile says the machine serves what git publishes.

supply_mismatch.summary: This host's installed registrations differ from the published declared supply.
supply_mismatch.why: A lane the host registers that git does not publish is capacity no consumer can discover; a lane git publishes that the host does not register is capacity consumers will route to and wait on forever.
supply_mismatch.remedy: Run `tartci fleet-macos verify-supply` for the per-lane verdicts. Reinstall from the checked-in profile (drain first), or commit the host's change and regenerate fleet/advertised-labels.json.
supply_mismatch.do_not: Do not edit fleet/advertised-labels.json by hand; it is regenerated from profiles/ and CI rejects a hand edit.

supply_unknown.summary: The installed registrations could not be compared with the published supply.
supply_unknown.why: An unreadable installed profile or published file, or a host_id the published file does not declare, leaves the comparison unanswered, which is not the same as a match.
supply_unknown.remedy: Run `tartci fleet-macos verify-supply` for the specific reason.

warm_vm_none.summary: No warm gate VM is parked on this host.
warm_vm_none.why: A warm VM is opt-in (lane key warm_vm) and off by default; when on, none is parked while the lane is serving, cooling down, or yielding to other demand.

warm_vm_parked.summary: A warm gate VM is parked under a memory-only lease.
warm_vm_parked.why: The opted-in lane pre-booted one VM to VM-up so the next job skips lease, clone and boot. It reserves memory and one macOS VM slot, no cores, and yields to other demand.
warm_vm_parked.remedy: Nothing to do. To stop it, remove the lane's warm_vm key and reload, or drain the pool.

warm_vm_stale.summary: The warm VM record is not being refreshed by a live supervisor.
warm_vm_stale.why: The supervisor that parked the VM exited or wedged without tearing it down. The VM and its lease may remain until the reaper or lease reclaim removes them.
warm_vm_stale.remedy: Run `tartci doctor --reap --json` under its ownership rules, confirm no parked VM remains in `tart list`, then delete ~/.tartci/state/warm-vm/parked.json.
warm_vm_stale.do_not: Do not delete a VM whose supervisor is still alive; check the pid first.

warm_vm_overdue.summary: The warm VM has been parked past its maximum park age.
warm_vm_overdue.why: The supervisor tears a parked VM down at TARTCI_WARM_VM_MAX_PARK_SECS on its next loop pass. Overdue means the loop is not passing, usually because the supervisor is stuck.
warm_vm_overdue.remedy: Inspect the lane log for the supervisor named in the record; reload the lane at an idle boundary if it is stuck.

warm_vm_unreadable.summary: The warm VM record could not be read.
warm_vm_unreadable.why: The record is malformed or unreadable, so whether a VM is parked is unknown.
warm_vm_unreadable.do_not: Do not read an unreadable record as no warm VM.
